correctness.rationale: The four-state transition matrix yields the previously published exact GTFT payoff, independently checked by a rational linear-system inversion. Independent iid sampling symmetrizes it to (b-c)/2 times a nonnegative moment-series gap. Jensen, convex chord bounds and strict equality of x^2 identify the universal sign, explicit variance certificate and both unique fixed-mean extremizers. 346 exact-rational program assertions corroborate but do not prove the uncountable-law claim. The proof covers 0<delta<1, b>c>0, independent iid strategies on [0,G], 0<G<=1.

value.rationale: Replacing an observed distribution by a representative mean strategy is a motivated approximation specifically compared numerically by the original IGT paper. The exact universal overestimation direction and unique fixed-mean worst-case law provide a mathematically sharp robustness limit from only mean and support data; nondegenerate stationary IGT laws retain a nonzero gap even as the population size grows. The result is more than one numerical example, a rephrasing of the payoff matrix or an arbitrary slice. It does not claim a universal evolutionary fitness effect.
